subject.title: [security] Non-admin WebVNC and egress bridges survive user-token revocation

question: Should Crabbox make active non-admin WebVNC and egress bridges fail closed immediately when the portal session, revoked-user list, or GitHub membership check invalidates that user?
rationale: The source supports the stale live-session gap, but the exact behavior affects security guarantees and long-lived bridge lifecycle semantics, so maintainers should choose the boundary before automation implements it.

options.title: Fix live bridge revocation
options.body: Store revocable session or GitHub identity metadata for non-admin WebVNC and egress bridges and close them when that identity is no longer authorized.

options.title: Document bounded stale sessions
options.body: Keep existing live bridges until disconnect or lease end and explicitly document that revocation applies only to new requests and Code viewer sessions.

options.title: Fold into broader bridge auth redesign
options.body: Keep this issue open under a larger WebSocket authorization pass covering Code, WebVNC, egress, control, restored sockets, and token revocation consistently.

recommendation.title: Fix live bridge revocation
recommendation.body: Store revocable session or GitHub identity metadata for non-admin WebVNC and egress bridges and close them when that identity is no longer authorized.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent history in the Worker auth, bridge revocation, and GitHub membership paths involved here.
